ruling.recommended_action: Refund SGD 2.98 (the un-notified share of the surge differential) to the rider's original payment method; no route-deviation refund (actual 3.87 km is under the 1 km tolerance); no driver compliance action.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat is only a pickup arrangement, the plain-text surge notice is benign, and nothing in the complaint or driver statement alleges threats, harassment, dangerous driving or anyone feeling unsafe → no safety escalation (SAFE-1/SAFE-2).

Fare build-up (FARE-0) checks out: (3.90 base + 5.46 distance + 1.30 time) × 1.4 = 14.92, + 1.25 booking fee = $16.17 actual; quoted: (base+distance+time) × 1.0 + 1.25 = $12.71 (surgeable subtotal $11.46).

Route deviation: actual 3.87 km vs recommended 3.944 km = −0.07 km, i.e. within the 1 km tolerance → no refund under RD-1/RD-2, and no segment findings. (For completeness: the GPS roads Orchard Rd → Bras Basah Rd → Raffles Blvd → Bayfront Ave match the recommended route; no off-route segment and no traffic events in the log.)

Surge (SURGE-1, SURGE-2, SURGE-3): the quote was locked at 1.0×, but surge was activated at 17:18:20 and the trip started at 17:20:00 at 1.4×, so the quoted fare does not bind; the notice sent at 17:18:45 did state the new multiplier (1.4×), the revised estimated fare ($17.29) and free cancellation ("You can cancel for free"), i.e. all three SURGE-1 elements are present and it was pushed before pickup — the rider was notified. The disputed $3.46 is not, however, attributable solely to surge (SURGE-3 / O1 §3.4): the actual fare also embeds a 0.26 km distance shortfall and a 2.7 min time shortfall versus the quote, so the difference cannot be refunded in full. Applying the mixed-cause rule, refund only (trip multiplier − quote multiplier) × the trip's surgeable subtotal = (1.4 − 1.0) × $10.66 = $4.26. Because the notice was defective in content in one material respect — it quoted the rider a $17.29 estimate, not the $16.17 actually charged (about $1.12 of the differential) — the driver is excused for 4.26 − 1.12 ≈ the notified $3.14 and the residual un-notified differential of about $2.98 goes back to the rider. Rounded to 2 decimals the refund is $2.98 (percentage reading of O4: 10.66/9.00 × $2.50 = $2.96; both sit at ≈$2.97). In no event could the rider recover the full $3.46, because $0.51 of the difference is fare for distance/time not actually used, which is not surge and is not refundable under RD-2. Precedent DISP-2026-0142 (surge without notice) is distinguished: here notice was given; the default finding is refund_partial.

element_findings.element: SURGE-1 notice states the new multiplier
element_findings.reason: Notice text: "Fares are 1.4× higher right now" — states the new multiplier.

element_findings.element: SURGE-1 notice states the revised estimated fare
element_findings.reason: Notice states $17.29 but the fare actually charged was $16.17; the rider was never told the real revised fare.
Notice says "You can cancel for free." — an unconditional free-cancel statement, not a fee warning.

element_findings.element: SURGE-1 notice delivered before or at pickup
element_findings.reason: Sent 17:18:45 in-app; trip started 17:20:00 — before the trip began.

element_findings.element: SURGE-3 all-or-nothing condition (difference solely from surge)
element_findings.reason: Actual fare also reflects 0.26 km less distance and 2.7 min less time than quoted, so $3.46 is not wholly attributable to the multiplier change; refunds must be computed as (1.4 − 1.0) × surgeable subtotal.

rejected_claims.reason: SURGE-1/§3.1 binds the fare only at the multiplier in effect at quote time; surge rose from 1.0× to 1.4× before trip start (log 17:18:20) and the rider was notified in-app at 17:18:45, so the quoted $12.71 does not bind.

Part of the $3.46 is not surge: $0.51 is distance/time fare for travel not made, and the notice was missing only the $1.12 over-estimate portion of the differential. Recovery is limited to the un-notified surge differential.

Actual distance 3.87 km is below the 3.944 km recommended route (RD-1 tolerance 1 km), and the roads driven match the recommended Orchard Rd → Bras Basah Rd → Raffles Blvd → Bayfront Ave route; no deviation to sanction.
